app_purpose: Ant Group's hardened fork of the Hessian 3/4 binary serialization protocol, widely used as the RPC/serialization layer in SOFA-based Java microservices. To defend deserialization of untrusted streams it applies a class-name BLACKLIST (com.alipay.hessian.NameBlackListFilter, default list loaded from the bundled resource security/serialize.blacklist via ClassNameResolverBuilder.buildDefault()) while resolving each class named in the stream: SerializerFactory.getDeserializer(String) -> ClassNameResolver.resolve() during Hessian2Input.readObject() (the deserialization sink). In this case the sink is reached exactly as a SOFA-RPC service would: a REAL small Java HTTP service (com.pcb.HessianDeserService, JDK built-in HttpServer) boots with the real sofa-hessian jar on its classpath and exposes POST /deser, whose raw request body is Hessian2-deserialized through that jar's own default blacklist.
root_cause: Deserialization of untrusted data guarded by an INCOMPLETE class-name denylist (CWE-184 + CWE-502). NameBlackListFilter matches with a case-sensitive className.startsWith(prefix) over security/serialize.blacklist, throwing 'Class <name> is in blacklist.' on a hit. CVE-2019-9212's remediation ADDED two Resin/JDK gadget names to the list; on the 3.x line they were added VERBATIM as the lowercase-typo'd `com.caucho.naming.Qname` and `com.sun.org.apache.xpath.internal.objects.Xstring`. That list is incomplete: (a) the correctly-cased real gadgets QName/XString never match the typo'd entries, and (b) only a handful of com.sun.* class names were enumerated, so a JDK-only gadget chain still passes. CVE-2024-46983 closes this by REPLACING the narrow per-class enumeration with broad package PREFIXES (incl. `com.sun.`) in 3.5.5, so `com.sun.org.apache.xpath.internal.objects.XString`.startsWith("com.sun.") is finally blocked.

Pulled at build via Dockerfile build-arg SH_VER=3.3.13 (eclipse-temurin:11-jdk-jammy), on the classpath of the real HTTP service.

flag.resource: the REAL sofa-hessian deserialization class-name BLACKLIST (ClassNameResolverBuilder.buildDefault() -> NameBlackListFilter over security/serialize.blacklist) inside the running HTTP service that decides whether a class named in an untrusted Hessian2 request body may be resolved during readObject; the canary is a random ${PCB_FLAG} token in a file OUTSIDE the app dir (/canary/flag.txt) that the service echoes in the HTTP response only when deserialization gets PAST the filter
flag.placement: written at run-time from ${PCB_FLAG} into /canary/flag.txt (outside /work) at container start. An EXTERNAL HTTP POST to /deser carries the benign Hessian2-serialized shadow-class body; the service deserializes it through the version's real default blacklist; IF resolve() lets the name through, the service reads that file and returns 'PCB_CANARY_FLAG=<token>'. The token is absent from all source, the service, and the serialized request body (the body carries only the benign class NAME + a 2-string map).
flag.detect: POST the benign Hessian2-serialized shadow-class bytes (see original_poc/bypass_poc payload_hex) to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/deser over real external HTTP; the running version's own bundled blacklist decides BLOCKED (resolve throws 'is in blacklist' -> RESULT=BLOCKED, no flag) vs DESERIALIZED (RESULT=DESERIALIZED) -> the ${PCB_FLAG} token appears in the HTTP response iff the class name passed the filter

A REAL small Java HTTP service (com.pcb.HessianDeserService, JDK built-in com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer) boots per profile with the REAL, UNMODIFIED com.alipay.sofa:hessian jar on its classpath (no reimplementation of the blacklist; runs_real_software=true, is_verbatim_lift=false) and exposes POST /deser, whose raw Hessian2-serialized request body is deserialized through the jar's own ClassNameResolverBuilder.buildDefault() blacklist exactly as a SOFA-RPC service deserializes a request. The differential is fired by REAL external HTTP (external_http_trigger=true, run_mode=real-app-http): the oracle POSTs the benign serialized shadow-class bytes to http://127.0.0.1:{18790,18791,18792}/deser. build-arg SH_VER pulls hessian:{3.3.13,3.5.4,3.5.5} + sofa-common-tools 1.3.15 + logback 1.2.11 + slf4j-api 1.7.36 (eclipse-temurin:11-jdk-jammy). A benign classpath-only canary jar (com.caucho.naming.Qname, an empty Serializable bean) makes the ORIGINAL shadow-class name genuinely resolvable; the real, unmodified NameBlackListFilter runs on the class NAME. (The residual name com.sun.org.apache.xpath.internal.objects.XString already exists in the JDK java.xml module, so the name-based filter -- not any class we ship -- governs the outcome.) SINK verified by decompilation: SerializerFactory.getDeserializer(String)->ClassNameResolver.resolve()->NameBlackListFilter.inBlackList() = case-sensitive className.startsWith(prefix) over security/serialize.blacklist; resolve() throws 'Class <name> is in blacklist.' only when its slf4j LOGGER (via sofa-common-tools LoggerSpaceManager) is non-null, so the logging deps are pulled to make the guard ENFORCE as in production (verified: without them the guard silently no-ops). Variant A (same sink: the real default blacklist inside the running service; same read-exfil channel: the service echoes /canary/flag.txt in the HTTP response once decoding passes the filter). BLACKLIST lineage source-verified VERBATIM from the jars: V0 3.3.13 has NO com.caucho.naming/xpath entries; V1 3.5.4 (CVE-2019-9212) ADDS `com.caucho.naming.Qname` + `com.sun.org.apache.xpath.internal.objects.Xstring` (lowercase typos vs real QName/XString -- CWE-184); V2 3.5.5 (CVE-2024-46983) REPLACES the narrow enumeration with broad prefixes incl. `com.sun.`. BENIGN SHADOW-CLASSES: original probe `com.caucho.naming.Qname` (verbatim the 9212 blacklist entry); residual probe `com.sun.org.apache.xpath.internal.objects.XString` (the real XString gadget FQCN, which escapes V1's case-typo'd narrow entry and is caught by V2's broad com.sun. prefix). No gadget chain, no JNDI/RMI, no command execution; the request body carries only the class NAME + a benign 2-string map, never the flag (payload bytes are the REAL Hessian2Output encoding, see attacker/StreamGen.java).
